chapter: Early life, family and Crescent Orchestra
title: Birth and musical family
summary: Born in Algiers in 1889, he names his uncles, a cornetist and a trombonist who was first to use the slide trombone.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape

blocks.x: Okay, Mr. Mineta, anytime you want to tell us about your life. Oh, gee. Oh, that's something.
Where were you born? Professor? Huh? Where were you born? I'm born in Algea. Want to know my boy? Yes, birthday. Yes, birthday. Well, my own Algea, Louisiana. Third day of October, 1889.
Who were some of your family? Were any of your family interested in music?

Oh, yes. My uncles, Jules and Melinda, and Dues. They were the professionals of the town. What did they play? Well, Jules and Melinda, he was a trumpet player. Well, during that time, they didn't say trumpet, it was cornich, you know. He was a cornich player. Brass, band, and orchestra. And my other uncle, he was a trombonist. He came from Canceritory, from France, down here. And he was the first man that ever known at Oak Steen with a sliding trombone.
You mean they were all the valve trombones before that?

Well, that's all they used to use, valve trombones. That was all the style of valve trombones. But he was the first one for the same. Okay. Jules had a nickname. Yes, he had a nickname. They called him Norm. Norm Manetta.
Norm? Norm, yeah. That's why I was wondering if that was the same man he mentioned. Well, that's it. What did you play your first job with?
